q6.answer: The worker locks the due schedule row with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED in the tick transaction, so only one worker processes a given schedule at a time and the other skips it. Then the active-run check and the insert cannot race. As a backstop, UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING stops a second run row for the same fire time.

q7.answer: It is kept in job_schedules.next_fire_at, in UTC. The tick moves it to the first fire time after now() once it has processed the schedule, and enabling a schedule or resuming a tenant recomputes it the same way, so missed fire times are never caught up.

q8.answer: A worker locks one claimable run (status pending, next_attempt_at <= now(), schedule enabled, tenant not paused) with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED in a single transaction. In that transaction it sets the run to running, increments attempt_count, inserts a run_attempts row with outcome running, and sets current_attempt_id. Locked rows are skipped by other workers, so no two workers start the same run.

q9.answer: The liveness state is run_attempts.last_heartbeat_at, which the worker refreshes every 30 seconds while outcome is running. Each tick's reaper looks for running attempts whose last_heartbeat_at is more than 2 minutes old, using the partial index on running attempts, and marks them presumed_dead.

q10.answer: The wait is recorded in job_runs.next_attempt_at, which is set to now() plus the backoff (1 minute after attempt 1, 5 minutes after attempt 2) when the run goes back to pending. The retry starts when a claim finds the pending run with next_attempt_at <= now(), the same as a first start. The backoff is counted from when the failure is recorded, which is still to be confirmed.

q11.answer: The job_runs row is recorded once per fire time, holding the schedule, fire_time, status and retry state. The run_attempts row is recorded once per execution try, holding the worker, start and heartbeat times, outcome and error. A run has at most 3 attempt rows, enforced by the UNIQUE (run_id, attempt_no) constraint.

q12.answer: Every worker write is guarded by WHERE id = :attempt AND outcome = 'running', and the attempt ID is the fencing token. Once the reaper has marked the attempt presumed_dead, the late report matches zero rows and writes nothing. The run row changes only in the same transaction, and only when the attempt update matched. The row lock makes a racing reaper and worker wait for each other, so the second one sees the outcome is no longer running.
